description.narrative:
PGA`s vision is to contribute to the creation of a rule-based international order for a more equitable, safe, sustainable and democratic world.
As a non-governmental, multiparty, international network of legislators, acting in their individual capacity PGA informs and mobilizes parliamentarians in all regions of the world to advocate for human rights and the Rule of Law, democracy, human security, inclusion, gender equality and justice, including climate justice.
PGA´s strategic plan 2022 -2024 consists of three programs:
- International Law and Human Rights (ILHR program)
- Gender, Equality and Inclusion (GEI program).
- International Peace and Security (IPSP program).
All Programs of PGA are organized into nine global international results-oriented campaigns with clear objectives.
The goal of the core campaign for "Democratic Renewal and Human Rights" is to inform , empower and mobilize parliamentarians to use their representative, legislative and oversight prerogatives to effectively tackle threats to democratic principles and institutions and human rights a the domestic, regional and international levels.
The ILHR program consists of three campaigns:
1) Campaign for the universality and effectiveness of the system of the Rome statue of the international criminal court.
2) Campaign for the abolition of the death penalty
3) Campaign for the Protection of the Oceans and Implementation of SDG 14
The goals of the campaigns are to contribute to ending impunity and improve access to justice for victims of the gravest international crimes and to work towards the abolition of the death penalty and to promote justice systems grounded in the rule of law.
The GEI program consists of three campaigns:
1) Campaign to end child, early and forced marriage
2) Campaign to end discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity
3) Campaign (regional) for a Human Rights-based approach to climate action
The goals of the campaigns are to sensitize and mobilize parliamentarians in the Caribbean around the Escazu agreement ( environmental treaty of Latin America and the Caribean), to contribute to the decriminalization of consensual same-sex conduct and to contribute to legislative and policy-making processes that ban child marriage and promote girl's equal access to education, health, justice and economic opportunities.
The IPSP program consists of two campaigns;
1) Campaign addressing the threat of weapons of mass destruction subdivided into:
a) Campaign for the Universality and Implementation of the biological and Toxin Weapons Convention and Implementation of UN security Council Resolution 1540
b) Campaign to Promote Nuclear and Radiological Security
c) Global Cybersecurity Initiative
2) Campaign on Addressing the Illicit Trade in small Arms and Light Weapons and Improved regulation of the International arms Trade
The goals of the campaigns are to marshalling global parliamentary support for ratification of relevant international treaties, as well as providing legal and technical advice relating to subsequent implementation and enforcement of these treaties at the national level.

Insatsen avser ett kärnstöd till Parliamentarians for Global Action (PGA) om totalt 9 MNSEK för att implementera sin strategiska plan "Empowering and mobilizing legislators as champions for human rights, democracy and a sustainable world” under perioden 2022-2024. Insatsen syftar till att mobilisera parlamentsledamöter att bidra till en internationell ordning baserad på internationella regelverk för en mer rättvis, säker, demokratisk och hållbar värld. Detta genom arbete mot 8 målområden: - Universalitet och effektivitet av Romstadgan av den internationella brottmålsdomstolen (ICC) och dess system - Universalitet och implementering av konventionen om biologiska och kemiska vapen (BWC) samt implementering av FN's säkerhetsrådsresolution 1540 (2004) - Förhindra den olagliga handeln med lätta vapen (SALW) samt förbättrad reglering av internationell vapenhandel för att förhindra övergrepp på mänskliga rättigheter - Stoppa barn- och tidiga tvingande äktenskap - Stoppa diskriminering på basis av sexuell orientering och genus identitet - Stoppa dödsstraffen - Skydd av haven och implementering av SDG 14 - Säkerställa att demokratiska normer, institutioner och civilt och politiskt utrymme, inklusive lagstiftares grundläggande rättigheter, är skyddade och uppehållna
PGA's totala organisationsbudget för projektperioden 2022-2024 är 62 MNSEK, av vilken PGA efterfrågar 9 MNSEK (14,5%) från Sida i kärnstöd. Den återstående delen planeras att täckas av medel från Danmark, Kanada, Nederländerna, Estland, Schweiz, Liechtenstein (Global Equality Fund), mellanstatliga organisationer som UNSCAR och EU kommissionen samt stiftelser och fonder så som Stewart R Mott Foundation, Arcus Foundation, CRDF Global, Oak Foundation, Open Society Foundations, Planethood Foundation, Raymond & Elizabeth Bloch Foundation och Sigrid Rausing Trust.

Parliamentarians for Global Action has applied to Sida for core funding of 9 million SEK to implement their plan "Empowering and mobilizing legislators as champions for human rights, democracy and a sustainable world” during the period 2022 - 2024 The intervention aims to mobilize legislators to contribute to a rules based international order for a more equitable, safe, sustainable and democratic world. PGA will work through campaigns focused at 8 overarching objectives: - Universality and Effectiveness of the Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court (ICC) system - Universality and Implementation of the Biological and Toxin Weapons Convention (BWC) and Implementation of UN Security Council Resolution 1540 (2004) - Addressing the Illicit Trade in Small Arms and Light Weapons (SALW) and Improved Regulation of the International Arms Trade to Prevent Human Rights Abuses - Ending Child, Early and Forced Marriage (CEFM) - Ending Discrimination based on Sexual Orientation and Gender Identity (SOGI) - Abolition of the Death Penalty (ADP) - Protection of the Oceans and Implementation of SDG 14 (to conserve and sustainably use the oceans, seas and marine resources) - Democratic Renewal and Human Rights The interventions total budget for the period 2022-2024 is estimated to 62 million SEK contributed by Institutional donors, Foundations and other Private entities.

Sida has supported PGA since 1996 and with core funding since 2003. PGA works with individual parliamentarians in their national contexts and parliaments, and then leverages that capacity with international networking to support democracy, human rights and peace. This is done through educating, sensitizing, building the technical capacity and strengthening the will of parliamentarians to take ownership, take initiatives and take legislative action.
2023 is the second year of PGA's strategic plan 2022 - 2024. The strategic plan incorporated the recommendations from the Sida supported external mid-term evaluation conducted by Rightshouse in 2021.
During the second year of the implementation of the Strategic Plan Sida expects in particular results on lower level objectives (output). The overall objectives will be assessed at the end of the Strategic Plan in 2024.
In 2023 some of the most important results from the nine global international campaigns are:
- Campaign for the Effectiveness and Universality of the Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court:
PGA launched a "Handbook for parliamentarians on the national nomination of Judicial candidates for the ICC". The handbook sets forth specific criteria and recommendations for parliamentarians to encourage their government to improve national nomination procedures for ICC judicial candidates and adopt good practices and requirements to ensure these processes are fair, transparent and merit based.
PGA continued to support and assist members in advancing the ratification of the Rome Statue in Armenia, Jamaica, Somalia and Ukraine. Notably Armenia deposited its instrument of ratification of the Rome statue in November, following PGA technical assistance, becoming the 124th State Party to the Court. PGA also contributed to the ratification of all the amendments on war crimes to the Rome Statue in Uruguay.
Campaign to end Child, Early and Forced Marriage
PGA members from Sierra Leone played a pivotal role in passing the "Prohibition of Child Marriage Act" in Sierra Leone (2024).
Campaign to End Discrimination Based on Sexual Orientation and Gender Identity
The Parliament of the Cook Islands passed a new criminal code, including decriminalization of homosexuality. PGA members from Cook Island played a pivotal role in passing the new legislation.
Campaign for the Abolition of the Death Penalty
The Parliament of Pakistan enacted the "Control of Narcotics Substance Act 2023", which abolishes the death penalty for drug trafficking convictions. PGA´s Death Penalty Campaign has been active in the country since 2016.
The Parliament of Malaysia adopted two bills abolishing the mandatory death penalty for 12 offences. This achievement represents the culmination of PGA members efforts in the country since 2012.
PGA does not allow membership from authoritarian counties and thus has no members/champions where capital punishment is prevalent, such as China, Iran and Saudi Arabia.
